=={{header|FreeBASIC}}==
Yes! FreeBASIC has a safer mode of execution.

Safe mode in FreeBASIC is activated using the <CODE>-lang fb</CODE> or <CODE>-lang deprecated</CODE> compilation flag, and provides the following restrictions:

# Does not allow direct use of pointers
# Disables direct memory access using <CODE>PEEK</CODE> and <CODE>POKE</CODE>
# Restricts the use of <CODE>ASM</CODE> (inline assembly code)
# Does not allow direct calls to operating system functions
# Limits the use of variables without explicit declaration
# Requires variable declaration with <CODE>DIM</CODE>
# Implements stricter array bounds checking

To activate this safer mode, compile like this:

<CODE>fbc -lang fb program.bas</CODE>

This mode is especially useful for educational environments or when greater control over the code is needed, although it should not be considered a total guarantee of security for code from untrusted sources.

The term '''"safer mode"''' is more accurate than "safe mode", since it does add layers of protection but does not guarantee absolute security.
